# Focused availability and household-context repeat — 2026-11-13

Runtime commit **`f304747` on master**, after committing PY-050 through PY-053. One authorized attempt each for Q02/Q04/Q07/Q08; no retries or semantic judge. All eleven stones were indexed in disposable Testcontainers with real qwen3-embedding:0.6b embeddings (1024 dimensions). Luna (`openai/gpt-6-luna`) parses, audits and extracts evidence; Nemotron Free (`nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free`) selects and answers. Questions, fifteen fixture/manifest hashes, model IDs and settings match the previous PY-052 run. Runtime source hashes still match the capture; offline report reproduction verified.

## Result

**The changes have not demonstrated the intended model improvement.** Q02's audit could not be evaluated because the grounding call failed. Household context still becomes mandatory compatibility in all three targeted granite scenarios. Q04 audit catches the mistake, Q07 audit is unavailable, and Q08 audit incorrectly accepts it.

The live capture test reports **1 passed** because all four requests returned HTTP 200 and were archived. That does not establish useful answers: execution integrity is **1 pass / 3 fail**; even the structural pass Q08 fails its condition and disposition expectations. Semantic answer judging remains disabled.

| Case | Previous PY-052 | Current result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q02 | Audit incomplete: redundant availability request demanded | Parse has no mandatory compatibility and no redundant status request. Grounding provider error; audit not run, so availability-fix outcome unknown. |
| Q04 | Audit catches spurious mandatory compatibility | Same error persists; audit also catches missing required candidate type. Both compound agreements survive. No candidate assessment. |
| Q07 | Audit complete; spurious required compatibility causes exclusion | Spurious required compatibility persists, using “Find one granite stone” as its quote; candidate type missing. Grounding provider error prevents audit and assessment. |
| Q08 | Audit complete; false granite agreement values and hard compatibility cause exclusion | Same semantic failures persist. Audit accepts invented mandate and grounding accepts non-applicable scope as false agreements. Sir Pebble excluded instead of conditional. |

For Q02 and Q07 the final state records `grounding_model_error` / `BadRequestResponseError`; Langfuse generation observations report **Provider returned error**. The parser DTO itself validated. The underlying provider cause is not established. Do not classify these as false coverage refusals, parser DTO errors, or successful fixes.

Q08 confirms the important distinction: Python applies the supplied hard-criterion policy consistently, but the model has supplied the wrong role/scope and the semantic audit failed to catch it. More schema wording alone was insufficient in this sample. Explicit hard compatibility must remain enforceable; silently dropping all compatibility requirements would hide the error.
